correctness.rationale: For a,b>=3, all distance-three pairs are exactly the deleted matching, allowing a proof of pairability for every even set of size at least four. Exhaustive domination cases, exact four-set inclusion-exclusion, and a reduction from larger mixed-shore sets to dominating four-subsets prove all coefficients. The algebraic crossover identity is verified symbolically. Direct graph-level checks over 61 instances and 58,819 nonempty subsets agree with all three polynomials.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General optimization algorithms do not imply a closed labeled distribution or inclusion-minimal classification. A paired-domination formula cannot subsume a semipaired formula because whole even shores qualify only for the latter.

value.rationale: The exact labeled count and full minimality classification for the natural three-parameter family K_{a,b} minus a matching go beyond scalar semipaired domination. The formulas identify unbounded minimal-cardinality gaps in crowns and a sharp, nonmonotone edge-restoration crossover: q_n(n-1)-q_n(n) changes sign between n=9 and n=10 despite monotonicity of feasible semipaired sets under added edges. These precise coefficients have a structural explanation and are not generic graph-class substitutions.
